text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Senior U.S. leaders say United States will have to play a different global role in President Clinton's second term.
- Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew and Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong file new suit against Tang Liang Hong for remakrs made on their purchases of Hotel Properties Limited apartments.
- Bill Gates, chairman and chief executive officer of Microsoft, says Malaysia's proposed Multimedia Super Corridor is not a threat to Singapore.
- Steven Chiang makes history by being first blind student to pass Singapore's Practical Law Course examination.
- IPC Corp's share price at record low following personal computer maker's announcement it could suffer losses of up to Singapore $45.5 million in relation to troubled South Korean subsidiary.
- Creative Technology's share price surges Singapore $2.70 or 15 percent to $21.70 following release of group's best ever quarterly results.
- Company said to be linked to Government of Singapore Investment Corp among five companies which bid 372.3 billion yen for rare piece of land in Tokyo.

- Amcol Holdings' judicial managers take enforcement action against Mauritian businessman Roland Maurel in attempt to recoup company's U.S. $39.6 million investment in proposed resort and property development.
- Philippine Supreme Court overturns Renong Bhd's winning bid for control of historic Manila Hotel in favour of local company, citing constitutional provisions that favour Filipinos.
- Time Telecommunications Holdings Bhd which runs Adam network announces wide-ranging handphone package to woo investors to its listing in second half of this year.
- OCBC Bank's share price plunges on news over weekend that merger talks between its Malaysian unit and Pacific Bank was off.
- IPC Corp's market capitalisation plunges Singapore $75 million to $485 million as counter resumes trading after being suspended since Thursday.
- Listed property developer Wing Tai Holdings' service apartments business is likely to go into full swing soon.
- Petroleum Nasional Bhd buys Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd's 43.75 percent stake in Dai Hung oil field in Vietnam.
